summary: Every part of this hypothesis, (a) to (e), is already on master: it came in through d7bf1c76 (hyp/bf16-readflush, which names this slug) and landed in 8f233e88 (scored bc147c5b, 1.2735). Its one real question, whether R=32 at 72 CTAs beats R=16 for qkv m=1 under a read flush, has been answered no in two checks (a3dcd4cb: R=32 read 1.016; a6424247: 1.029 / 1.043). Running it again would rebuild master and measure nothing new; move it to done as superseded / landed-and-killed.
justification: Master's B12_CELLS['qkv_gate'] already lists the R=32 challengers (0,8,1,8,32) and (1,8,1,4,32); B12_INST_R, the per-R encode, CELL_FLUSH_MODES / flush_mode='read' in _cell_gate, B12_GATE_FLUSH='read', B12_CHALLENGER_MARGIN=0.03, _b12_pick and the re-printed gate lines are all there (submission.py ~2976-2988 names this slug). In a6424247, R=16 inst 2 read 0.950 (10.34 / 10.88 us); R=32 inst 0 read 1.029, inst 1 1.043: both fail the read gate. a3dcd4cb gave R=32 at 1.016. The write-flush flattery the hypothesis predicted was confirmed (qkv 0.953 read vs 0.884 write) and that fix has landed. The sizing was marginal from the start (-1 to -2 us, below the 1.24% one-run margin).
confounders: 8f233e88 (read-flush gates + pooler khalf b2) contains the hypothesis's whole change: a rebuild would be an empty diff.

combo-rowowner-reduce-free-m1-qkv-o-plus-naive is the source of the R=16 row-owner shape; on master the bulk12 R=16 cell (5325ea40) beats the raw bulk cell under the read gate, a stronger incumbent than assumed.
interference: No companions; nothing new would be measured. Keeping R=32 alive needs a different shape (R=32 at 2 CTAs/SM with a smaller ring, or a split-K pair so 144 CTAs carry R=32 tiles): a new hypothesis.
open_questions: Retire this queue file to done/ (landed via d7bf1c76/8f233e88; R=32 killed by gate in a3dcd4cb and a6424247).
Gate noise in the incumbent column is ~1 us between variants of the same cell; should _cell_gate share one incumbent measurement across a cell's variants?
